Status: Wave 279 accepted (6.3): the Falcon message-transport state machine Class738

Method.evidence: Class738 is the message-transport state machine that sends one application-layer message at a time and waits for its confirmation (states IDLE, WAIT_CON). Its static constructor builds an 8-entry transition table, and the handlers name themselves: d logs HandleRequest and sends through b(Class818); c logs QueueRequest {1} and enforces get_QueueLimit (with the Queue overflow and Max queue length messages); e logs Received {1}, records the frame with the receiving-sequence service and publishes the Class750/Class822 event; smethod_0 is a single Task.CompletedTask for the entries that leave IDLE unchanged; b(Class738,Class818) logs Conf after {1} ms; a(Class738,Class818) logs ConfTimeout after {1} ms; a(Class738) logs Send next message from queue (age={1}ms). The send path b(Class818) logs Send {1} / Sending {1} succeeded/failed and defers with Defer send by {1} ms because of MinTimeBetweenSend, which named the method_17 getter and its setter outright; a(Class818) is the per-frame wait time computed from BusInterfaceConfiguration.IsRfMulti, the TPCI bits and the frame length (65535/14850/5850/2850 ms); a(Class818,bool) is the confirmation publisher both confirmation handlers call.
Method.themes: The state-machine pattern now covers two Falcon machines (Class733 in wave 278, Class738 here): the transition table plus each handler own log names every row, and the send path log named a setting the protected Bus facade had left opaque. Remaining rows of Class738 are left unresolved with reasons: the bool settings method_19 and e are only consumed by the SDK-protected Bus accessors w() and v(), and the Task<State> accessors a(Class738)/b(Class738,Class818) belong to the same table entries whose trigger enum is obfuscated (Class738/a a..d). Class737 is the same pattern with 25 free handlers and an obfuscated trigger enum E00..E27, so its handlers need the same table-plus-log reading next.
